issue_context.title: Implement PreFilter for VolumeZone plugin for performance
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add a PreFilter endpoint to the VolumeZone plugin to do all the operations that don't depend on the node, like listing the claims.

Also, the volumeZoneLabels set is wasteful. Having only 4 elements, it can be stored in a list. We can iterate through this list instead of iterating over the labels of a node or a PVC.

The list contains beta labels that are now deprecated. Can we remove them now?

### Why is this needed?

Performance :)

@liggitt can we remove support for `failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region` and the equivalent for zone? It's marked as deprecated since 1.17

This one is similar to #114075 if I'm understanding correctly.
I think I can help with this one.
/assign

If possible, add unit level benchmarks to prove that we are doing better after the changes.
See for example:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8f2371bcceff7962ddb4901c36536c6ff659755b/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/podtopologyspread/scoring_test.go#L1272

> @liggitt can we remove support for `failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region` and the equivalent for zone? It's marked as deprecated since 1.17

what does removing support mean? you can assume all nodes have the GA zone/region labels now, but you can't assume all references to the zone/region labels (in selectors, affinity, etc) have been updated to use the GA labels

For this particular node Filter, we get the topology labels of a PV and we ensure that the node has the same topology labels.

Can we assume that all PVs have the GA labels?

> Can we assume that all PVs have the GA labels?

I don't know... where do PVs get labels from?
I would expect they come from vendors. @msau42 ?
Then no, we cannot assume PVs have GA labels :-/
Can we put a stronger deprecation warning starting from 1.27 so that we can remove them in the future?

We're emitting warnings in 1.25+ as of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108554, but dropping support means existing persisted objects would just break on upgrade, right? I don't think we would do that.

Somebody may have created the PVs years ago with the beta labels. We don't actively backfill the objects with the GA labels. However, in csi migration logic we translate beta labels into GA labels: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/70617042976dc168208a41b8a10caa61f9748617/staging/src/k8s.io/csi-translation-lib/plugins/in_tree_volume.go#L202

However this only covers intree volume plugins. If any external drivers were depending on the label, then they would not be covered by this path, although they probably would have been broken by now if we stopped putting beta labels on Node objects?
I created https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268 to continue the discussion on beta zone label handling

review_comments: let's return immediately if `podPVTopologies` is empty. This is possible because a Pod might have ConfigMap/Secret volumes, but not PVs.
ConfigMaps and Secrets are still declared as Volumes and don't have PVs. But you are right... this already short-circuits
